notes: THE RULE HAS TWO HALVES AND BOTH ARE PINNED. The REJECTING half is discharged by the GENERAL FORMAT, not by a screen: 5.5 rule 1 makes every integer-n 'a fixed-point integer literal that shall be unsigned and nonzero unless otherwise specified in the associated rules', the format spells integer-2 with the grammar's unsigned integerLiteral, and a minus sign is therefore refused at parse (the negative golden). SR7 is precisely the 'unless otherwise specified' override, and it lifts the NONZERO half only - so the PERMITTING half is that FROM 0 shall compile and a zero-length record round-trip, which the two positive goldens measure on a sequential file and a relative one (Annex A.3 item 43 names both), at 2023 and at 2002. The override first appears in ISO/IEC 1989:2002 (13.16.41.2 SR6); the 1985 text has no such rule and its clause III.2 bars a zero integer, so --std 85 refuses FROM 0 (COBOL2386, IntegerOperandRules.RecordClause's ZeroFrom(2002), kb/Work PB5196; the 1985 negative golden pb5196-record-varying-zero-minimum-1985). Annex E carries no entry for this between 2014 and 2023. retired-witness: conformance:cases/13.18.43-RECORD/pb721_zero_length_record_85 (the program was the accepted-at-85 twin of the zero-length record; the 1985 text has no rule permitting zero (kb/Work PB5196), so it is renamed pb721_zero_length_record_2002 and accepted from 2002 on)
